# FDG9172

> CONSIDER naming the `out` parameter that reports the number of values successfully processed by an `OperationStatus` method “bytesConsumed,” “charsConsumed,” or “valuesConsumed” (as appropriate to the data type).

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.12.4 Partial Writes to Buffers and OperationStatus.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9172
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library suggestion, application suggestion, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Name the out parameter '{0}' of '{1}' '{2}'

The text has no body; the body of FDG9173 gives the expected signature. FDG9172 reports the out parameter that reports the number of input values processed by an externally visible method that returns OperationStatus when its name is not the one for the element type of the input buffer (found as for FDG9171; a string has char elements): bytesConsumed for byte and sbyte, charsConsumed for char, valuesConsumed for any other type. The parameter is the first of exactly two out parameters of an integer type, or the second when the first ends with Written and the second with Consumed (the order FDG9173 reports). Methods with one or more than two such out parameters, methods without an input buffer, overrides and interface implementations are not checked, so coverage is partial. Span<T> and Memory<T> types need .NET Core 2.1 or later, or the System.Memory package on .NET Framework and .NET Standard 2.0 (see FDG9137). Renaming a public parameter breaks callers that pass it as a named argument, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.
